PL T5 pt.6 ThE proverbs in this volume were collected in various towns in the Asaba district from natives of the towns. Noattempt has been made to systematise the transcription in view of the fact that differences of pronunciation exist between town and town. igbo_raw: Onu ite ades' ite akbp (Uk.).

igbo_raw: Ala di okporho n'obi adekwe warhapu enqëibe (0.0.).
english_raw: A woman's breast does not let men keep far from her. When a poor man depends on (sponges on) rich man and won't be driven away.

igbo_raw: Amwadi adana obwei nwa (0.0.).
english_raw: A rich man does not take a poor man's child

igbo_raw: Odafi ádana obwei nwa (0.0.).
english_raw: A rich man never takes away a poor man's child. A poor man can say this in misfortune.

igbo_raw: Qsa fu afa agona iwa (0.0.).
english_raw: If squirrel sees a name, he names a child. When a man admires rich man's house (has no money to build in same way).

igbo_raw: Qnp ani akpat' igwe aka (0.0.).
english_raw: He sits down and touches the sky. A rich man sends and his work is done.

igbo_raw: Ow(a) ägwunà (0.0.).
english_raw: The world does not finish. (Your children may suffer for you.) If a rich man harasses a poor man for nothing.

igbo_raw: Iyi àtá, obodi ebu azp n'enugu (0.0.).
english_raw: The stream dries up, a fool kills fish on the hill. Good things always go to the rich.

igbo_raw: Óbwei nwura oii; odafi analaiya (0.0.).

igbo_raw: Cakadaka ädäkg n' gbwqlg di oci (As.).
english_raw: A little palm wine stops in the calabash of the palm wine maker. A rich man is never reduced to poverty.

igbo_raw: Mwady ama nweke ebwebwe n' gnu mili anamwa n'iru eze (Ubul.).
english_raw: If a man has life, the rain (? saliva) will not beat the front of his teeth. Child of rich man will not go under in palaver.

igbo_raw: Qkûmn nabp iyili n'ozg ie, webde nno ijiji (As.).
english_raw: Two lame men walking in the road, killed four hundred flies. If two rich men travel, each makes his own arrangements.

igbo_raw: Ainyi je b' odafe, k'ainyi by; onye je b'obwei akalimwa (Ala).
english_raw: We go to the house of a rich man, that we may become so; who goes to poor man is better off. The poor are more generous than the rich.

igbo_raw: Qnodo ofu etiti nato ola (As.).

igbo_raw: Ainya adigo onye ala ka lie ngwele ; onebp ung oganozi lie (As.).
english_raw: A madman desires to eat a lizard; there is no house to eat it in. Not all can become rich

igbo_raw: Eze kbe ikße, oiyalu gnuma, eze kwupute qnuma, ani agwua n' aka (Uk.).
english_raw: The king complains, he stops vexation; if the king speaks out his wrath, the town finishes in his hand. When rich oppresses poor.

english_raw: Whose yams are done, let him eat, let him leave knife of child of poor man which he has in his hand to him. When rich and poor quarrel, poor man says this. B 2

igbo_raw: Nwofo adamwa onye kwo isi (As.).

igbo_raw: Ónyé Qiwe, mw' Ibé éngê (Ala).

igbo_raw: Nke afy onye adafy ibe (Ubul.).

igbo_raw: Orhõe gbuka mbwada, mwa umpa ang d'ibe (Uk.).

igbo_raw: Ani ádekoko elu onye na ntutße eluke (Uk.).

igbo_raw: Onye aiyiyo eiu ifele (As.).

english_raw: nisi oto (I.A.). Falling does not throw away things in stomach; who falls takes up his and stands up. (a) If child speaks without being asked. (b) Strangers don't understand each other as friends do.

english_raw: buya (O.0.). Olgigbwo says to child don't kill me, for three years you take to cut him up. Warning to child not to violate customs.

english_raw: gat' oka otpmi (0.0.). Death kills one that sacrifices person ; one who looks on says he will livo (bite corn) longer. By a man who gives up work.

igbo_raw: Obu obwa ji onwe n' anwu (As.).

igbo_raw: Ife onye alo b'ubwue (0.0.).

igbo_raw: Ogo aiyo plu di aiyo glu (Uk.).

igbo_raw: Ene meli pkulo, pne buluje ogunrhi (Uk.).

igbo_raw: Nwa Bu onye, iwa ka wagamukwa (Uk.).

igbo_raw: Ibwarikpu adeby amwam' ife uzg (Uk.).
english_raw: Those who run out at a shout are not the wiser ones. One who has work to do begins before helpers come.

igbo_raw: Fadebu ibi abw' af' alo n'ani (Ubul.).
english_raw: They don't carry elephantiasis to divine on the ground. When busy man is called for other work.

igbo_raw: Oti aky ti akq, nke bu iõele abia nal' oup (Ubul.).

igbo_raw: Anp any nni amwaya nonana n' oinya (Ubul.).

igbo_raw: Okike by olu, pwa bu oly (As.).

igbo_raw: Ainyakbo nni na dinweniye n'isi n' oyir(g) eyi (As.).
english_raw: Eyes that spoil go to head of owner and are not lost. When wife bears no children; she has other work.

igbo_raw: Omi dikana mili ogana nto (Uk.).
english_raw: A well that does not hold water, will hold ashes. When a man's wife bears no children, he does not repudiate her.

igbo_raw: Azq-nwe mili, mw' pdafy néa oji awp ary (Ala).
english_raw: A fish has water but sees no soap to wash with. A farmer may have many yams but no wife.

igbo_raw: Akwy leni bur' oka okwu (Uk.).
english_raw: Rotten nut brings palaver for the corn. Woman brings trouble to'man.

igbo_raw: Ainyi amwanwe ikg inibe Awolg nibe ewu; ngi by onye oica rwe ike inibe awolg nib' ewu (Uk.).
english_raw: We cannot tie leopard nor goat; you are a white man, you can tie leopard and goat. (a) Only white man can order obi. b) Leopard and goat (husband and co-respondent) come to court together, eat together.

igbo_raw: Ekwu kwemefu mak' ökwdmökwú; idumu, amwargn ebe dim nozi (Ubul.).
english_raw: I speak it as a word that is said ; idumu, I do not know where my husband is. Husband has never cohabited with wife, though he does with others.

igbo_raw: Qkoko mwa omwa etiwe ite, etiwe obobwa, n' omwago ebe ojekp alaru (Ubul.).
english_raw: Fowl wilfully breaks pot and open pot knows where it goes to sleep. When woman runs from husband; " they will return her."

igbo_raw: Di adina mwa nwunye adjna mwa (Ubul.).
english_raw: A husband is not good, a wife is not good. Six of one to half a dozen of the other.

igbo_raw: Qdidi n' onyny dièe (As.).
english_raw: It is not the same thing to be a lover and to be a husband. (? Waiting and marrying.)

igbo_raw: Di na nwunye l' ung debel' okwu (As.).
english_raw: Husband and wife build house for palaver.

igbo_raw: Nkwi ádäc' akd pkwye (ike) amwarg (As.).
english_raw: Palm tree is not ripe, foot (buttocks) does not know. The people of an ebo know when a man comes to marry a girl. SecRETS.

igbo_raw: Ume welunye okporo adenwe ísi (0.0.).
english_raw: Counsel they take with a woman has no head. When a man betrays a secret.

igbo_raw: Oke pfia gwa oke unq si na nkpodo di na rgiga (As.).
english_raw: The bush rat tells the house rat that (fish) basket is over the fire. If a man reveals secrets.

igbo_raw: Odiß eze bp eze (As.).
english_raw: A king's servant is king.

igbo_raw: Nwata bwakute eze olisi (Uk.).
english_raw: Child who runs to king has freedom.

igbo_raw: Obwome ádebu onye wa geji oru ni (Uk.).
english_raw: A witch does not kill one whom they take slave to bury. Stranger must go to house of obi; obi's child is a big man.

igbo_raw: Ajali si: naiya geje gafy Oba rwanng; n'obue gmwaka
english_raw: odomerhie gmwaka (I.A.). Axe says: he will go to see Oba his brother; if he kills him it is good; if he keeps him it is good. When a chief calls a young man.

igbo_raw: Ajii mul' umy si nke bu umwa sole si mili; nke nebuly umwa si enu (As.).
english_raw: A crocodile bears children, says her own follow her to the water; those that are not hers go up. (Ngwelanwu (lizard) is said to be child of aji.) etc.).

igbo_raw: Okwezé kwudi onye, onüe nkpuly iyi (0.0.).
english_raw: The word of the king meets one, he swallows iyi ball (stone). If the head chief accused a man, the accused admitted his guilt, whether innocent or guilty.

igbo_raw: Eze nwe anjnéa (0.0.).
english_raw: The head chief has the land. Wheu people excuse themselves from coming to head chief.

igbo_raw: Orhimili 1 li onye, olie ogu aya (0.0.)
english_raw: A river drowns one, it drowns his war medicine. To a reckless man who does not care for his chief.

igbo_raw: Qta dig' çwu k'ozi Qn'onu mw' pfurg onye iyibeni (Ala).
english_raw: A goat wants to put small calabash on his neck but does not see one to tie it on. No one can refuse to be made obi at no cost to himself.

igbo_raw: Wadeji qlopo nebuci фxQ (I.A.).
english_raw: They don't take olopo tree to shut the road. If two men are good friends, and a son commits adultery with the wife of one, it does not cause a quarrel. E

igbo_raw: Alo oke ta nab' plie; ngwel' asj: wazinye ego gow°
english_raw: çze (I.A.). Bite that rat bites turns to disease; lizard says: lend him money to file his teeth. Friends meet at night to talk; then tell a tale that causes laugh.

igbo_raw: Orhene Bu mbwada otã n'arh qzg (O.0.).
english_raw: When hunter kills duiker, he says "another year" (he will kill). A friend takes a friend's things and tells him.

igbo_raw: Ewu, nodibe ji, obug lie (0.0.).
english_raw: If a goat sits near yams it takes and eats. Cultivate a friend if you want benefactions.

igbo_raw: Onye jegebu si udene akala gini ijel ufe, mw'gb ebune
english_raw: geli anoa (0.0.). One who goes to be killed says to vulture: why do you fly over me, if qba does not kill me, you can't eat me. If friend calumniates son-in-law, man cannot take away daughter.

igbo_raw: AkBom' idide, olu asusy gelieye (I.A.).
english_raw: If they gather worms, work of eutting bush will eat them. If friends stay long to talk, the visitor can say this.

igbo_raw: Afy ifolo okqëi wawal' ubwo (I.A.).
english_raw: They see the light of a dry season, they cut the farn. A reply to 807. We will talk again on occasion.

igbo_raw: Aka nkponkpo ekwene nwanega kw'ote (0.0.).
english_raw: A short hand does not allow a tortoise to make a path. When a man cannot return a friend's kindness, he is ashamed and loses his friend.

igbo_raw: Okwu di n' ony ka mji amwa os) (As.).
english_raw: Word in mouth, that I take to know a friend. If friend deceives.

igbo_raw: Ngwele sibè k'oweli qdo nu ggo ; onye nabg ewe n' onu kwu (Uk.).
english_raw: One lizard says to another: let's fight with tails ; let neither take his mouth to speak. When friend injures friend, latter says this.

igbo_raw: Onye we mwady tinye n'iwele abprg qsia (Uk.)
english_raw: Who takes a man and puts him in trouble is not his friend.

igbo_raw: Mbwada si ibewa : onye ny muke muke, ya mukenye ibewe na akbukbg ibewe ka waji kwegwu (Uk.).
english_raw: Duiker says to his kin: who hears "hunter" let him tell his fellows, because skin of his kin they take to make drum. To friend who omits to warn.

igbo_raw: Nwene afugo ump nwene, Koji gedede umudte (Ubul.).
english_raw: When sister has seen the children of her sister, she embraces her husband's children. A man tells his friend, not his brother, and is killed.

igbo_raw: Onye olia énw os' (As.).
english_raw: A sick man has no friend.

igbo_raw: Wa nabo neso oiyi isi n' ainya (As.).
english_raw: They are friends like head and eyes. (Eyes don't see head) one doesn't know one's friend's secret.

igbo_raw: Elibe adakw' qnuma (As.).
english_raw: When you eat, you are not vexed. When a man refuses help but makes use of friend. HOME.

igbo_raw: Onye ninwerg nwunye ya by ikßd di ebo (Ala).
english_raw: Who has no wife is the poor man of his ebo. When a man returns home after work. E 2

igbo_raw: Nti pua obôdo; gmp oku (0.0.).
english_raw: Ears go to town hear a word. The stay at home does not know what happens.

igbo_raw: Qdidi n' oning diùe (As.).
english_raw: Staying in a place and living there are different.

igbo_raw: Onçh' ototo; adadimwa ikpenabg (0.0.).
english_raw: Let it be in the morning; it will not be good; twice (to-morrow). A man changes his mind after asking a friend to come and finish matter.

igbo_raw: Onye noka okg ptonye onp (Ubul.).
english_raw: Who stays long on message, he utters a word. To those who come to listen unasked.

igbo_raw: Gadi egede uno, ainyi eti ony (I.A.).
english_raw: Drum will be house, we beat mouth. If one man speaks when another should speak.

igbo_raw: Mbeku amanwe ofu akwa owelekw' awe (Ubul.).
english_raw: If a tortoise has only one cloth he does not take it to sew" dress. To man who begs for unique thing.

igbo_raw: Aceme ka ngwele bw'aku, anqrho bedi (0.0.).
english_raw: They wait for lizard to get hair, and don't go to a husband. To get rid of importunate beggar.

igbo_raw: Wadafia okba ntutu (Ubul.).
english_raw: They never flatter one who plants hair. To importunate borrower.

igbo_raw: Wasí obwodi na di and; onényo ainyanwu (Ala).
english_raw: They say to the fool that the day is done; he looks for the SUN. • When a man is twice refused and persists.

igbo_raw: Adas' Obolo pdikaby ebo onyefy (Uk.).
english_raw: They don't say Obolo (town), while it is not one's ebo. To one who interferes with domestic affairs of another.

igbo_raw: Ozq oyiyi ademe izizi (0.0.).
english_raw: A fresh corpse is not an ugly sight. When corpse's relatives do not attend funeral.

igbo_raw: Ozq ámy isi onwe (As.).
english_raw: A dead body cannot smell itself.

igbo_raw: Ifele ademe ozu (As.).
english_raw: A corpse feels no shame.

igbo_raw: Agu bul' onye abul' onyinyue (As.).
english_raw: Leopard carries off' someone, it carries his shadow. Shadow dies with man.

igbo_raw: Qrwu énwe eb¢le (As.).
english_raw: Death has no pity.

igbo_raw: Onwu ka mwa kalia ili antitia (As.).
english_raw: Death is better than long sickness.

igbo_raw: Qrwu ádênw jgú (As.).
english_raw: Death has no medicine.

igbo_raw: Ony' ek' grwu fijt (As.).
english_raw: Death refuses no one.

igbo_raw: Okwu enu grwene mbana, rta ainyi ej' ozo fe ainyike webueie ofu yzg (Uk.).
english_raw: The word of the world has no two roads, we should have gone to the blacksmith to sharpen an axe to shut one way. When mourner thinks of suicide. DEBT.

igbo_raw: Orhue adabwa ife onafuna ainya (Ubul.).
english_raw: The hunter does not shoot what he does not see. A man cannot pay what he did not see.

igbo_raw: Ekosiem bwa ukwy n'aka çte (0.0.).
english_raw: When one is ready to wrestle, leg and hand are far. If a man cannot find money to buy what he needs and wants to borrow though he is a notorious debtor.

igbo_raw: Cem ka ntukBo mili, amwana nke ei menye (Ala).
english_raw: " Wait for me to bathe" does not know what ci has done to him. A man who can wash quickly (i.e., has no sore) does not realise his good fortune.

igbo_raw: Ji nodo n'ubwo olue oluamba (Uk.).
english_raw: Yams stay in farm, they get good seed. One who lives long meets with good fortune.

igbo_raw: Mwo emekei adadi mwa ngelengele (Ubul.).
english_raw: When man uses bad climbing rope.

igbo_raw: Nkg &fj onye àdáfy ibe (0.0.).
english_raw: What troubles one does not trouble another. Tastes differ. Uf. 408, 664.

igbo_raw: Adeji aka arhainye mwady oiyi (0.0.).
english_raw: They don't choose a friend for a man. Tastes differ.

igbo_raw: Ife onye nwe, ibe aderiwe Nzizi y akwa, iigwele bw' oto
english_raw: (0.0.). A thing one has, the other has not. A fly has cloth, a lizard goes naked. People think differently.

igbo_raw: Ogo ejune adabwa mnie (As.).
english_raw: The combat of snails is bloodless. " You cannot suit me. DeFIANCE.

igbo_raw: Okbanko bwata anasi oba pla nyyi (As.).
english_raw: If woodman goes to head wife of Oba, he sleeps in the cold. If one man tries to injure another ; " it. is useless."

igbo_raw: Ako je n' okute, adienwolo (As.).
english_raw: The arrow that hits a stone is not sharp (again). A doctor cannot poison a doctor; i.e., you can't harm me.

igbo_raw: Enyi ádanwu tinye akwy wanabwa ebwe (Uk.).
english_raw: Elephant does not die in field they shoot him. When one threatens another, latter replies.

igbo_raw: Ofu onye aburg ani (Ala).
english_raw: One man is not a town. When a man disregards public opinion.

igbo_raw: Iyi oica eBunem, nem' iyi ofi (Ubul.).
english_raw: White alose doesn't kill me, what will black alose do? When man disregards big alose, he disregards small.

igbo_raw: Qbuna dibia ca mbwada ca ene (Ubul.).
english_raw: It is not a doctor that washes duiker and buck. To man who threatens to poison one.

igbo_raw: Kekenta si na rwata naey K'osi k' gbuye ya naëy mbumby fagente (Ubul.).
english_raw: A snake says if a child seeks thing to kill him, he seeks edge of street where they will bury him (child). To man who threatens to poison one.

igbo_raw: Agwg adeje kwalalasd (As.).
english_raw: Snake does not go straight away. If someone challenges : "you cannot easily beat me."

igbo_raw: Onye neli nkonwe nk'gninwerg &nägwßà (Ala).
english_raw: A man who eats what he has, his desire is for what he has nOU

igbo_raw: Qdig' onye n'uée; mw' aka adeluzie eme (Ala).
english_raw: It is in one's mind; but hands are not there to do it. If wishes were horses.

igbo_raw: Okul' onye onwß ndidi (0.0.).
english_raw: It reaches one who has patience. When young man becomes by death the oldest in idumu.

igbo_raw: Adawe ei mwo iwata akali Izoiya.
english_raw: They don't take title earlier than Izoiya. (Izoiya got yaws after taking title.) To a man aiming at okpala title in youth.

igbo_raw: Onye nepe mpeji, nagg orwe alo (Ala).
english_raw: Who plants small seed yam, deceives himself. Give up designs that are too big.

igbo_raw: Obwibu adebu ani (As.).
english_raw: A carrier cannot carry the earth. To one who tries impossibilities.

igbo_raw: Oti ukwu adeti ani (As.).
english_raw: A fighter cannot fight the earth. To one who tries impossibilities.

igbo_raw: Agadi lie, okwel' ggo (0.0.).
english_raw: Old man eats, he agrees to fight. A man is induced to risk his life when he has something to gain.

igbo_raw: Mbeku adali okbo (As.).
english_raw: A tortoise cannot climb a throne (ukb'o). When a man tries something beyond him. EXpErIence.

igbo_raw: Ainyi afugo nno mwadu, ainyi adakpozi ogo mwad' ili
english_raw: ife (I.A.). We see four hundred men, we do not call two hundred men anything. One does not go out to see a smaller thing than one has already seen.

igbo_raw: Mby m'onye; owd abg mwal' ife (0.0.).
english_raw: First (thing) does one; the second (time) he knows it. A man learns by experience.

igbo_raw: Onye jeluka, qfuluka (As.).
english_raw: Who walks far, sees much.

igbo_raw: Ibebune riwa Nwomg si n' etukw ani kbg okarga iyime
english_raw: onwe ainya; okhonarhina onye ku pte (I.A.). Ibebune, son of Nwomo, says that who stoops and beats drum observes himself; he beats better than one who stands. People observe what their fellows do.

igbo_raw: Owa nka ainyi puta wa' adeji zi giwe eni adaka (Uk.).
english_raw: This world we come to, they never take enwe to bury adaka. When monolinguals of different tongues meet, they don't kill each other. Uhwe aud adaka are species ot monkey.

igbo_raw: Ofia asp akBa ya epune elo (Uk.).
english_raw: If a bush forbids bag, it must not grow fungus. One who does not wish to be abused, does not abuse. (Do as you would be done by.)

igbo_raw: Ndi ainyampi nabp zu n' y20, ofu ainy' gro ibakekbe ofu ainy' oro n' ibakanni (Ubul.).
english_raw: Two half blind men meet by the way, one no left eye, one no right eye. Don't ask others to do what you won't do yourself.

igbo_raw: Akanne kwo akekpe; akekpe akwo akanni (As.).
english_raw: The right hand washes the left and ayenward. Of mutual respect.

igbo_raw: Aju nabo gjibu' aga k'eji bu gmunwa ; omunwa adiak' aga n'aju (As.).
english_raw: Two head pads carry sterile woman, they carry a fruitful woman; fruitful woman does not pass sterile with pad. When fruitful woman boasts to sterile woman, two men carry her when she dies, whether she has children or not.

igbo_raw: Ani nãa amazu K' ego aka mwa fa abuna imalegwe
english_raw: (I.A.). The whole country does not meet and tie cowries while they are not imalegwe. When two meet and quarrel; one boasts of his cowry wristlet.

igbo_raw: Okoko si kpankpana, obuly nojege nuye, ya nuege na ya amwan(a) omwa èu aju nyeya n'ainga (Ala).
english_raw: Fowl says to butterfly, if he is going to swallow him, swallow him at once, let him not wilfully make him giddy. No answer to repeated threats.

igbo_raw: Ogini bwago je enynkwy qsi ozinzi zienyi; ya nekwu pkbete naiya geje ckwu gmu (Ala).
english_raw: The rat runs up oil palms, says he sends messenger to elephant, let him root out sugar cane, that he goes to root out young palm leaves.

igbo_raw: Ofu ikpulako adiefq n' pky (As.).
english_raw: One nut is not lost in the fire. Of boaster.

igbo_raw: Ojtje Jê mwg (As.).
english_raw: You cannot walk to the other world. To boaster.

igbo_raw: K' onye rha k' odà ya k' adakada ji la nwunye ngwele rha iikpplego (Ubul.).
english_raw: Let one pay according to one's size; dung beetle cohabits with lizard's wife and pays one cowry fine. To boaster.

igbo_raw: Okegwu adetenerhi ngwesi (0.0.).
english_raw: A dancer does not dance better than ngwesi (yellow wagtail). To boaster.

igbo_raw: Wadebu iru aka onye anwulu eme (Ubul.).
english_raw: They don't feel cross more than one who has smoke (in his face). Two rich men boasting.

igbo_raw: Qtonto adato gko isi (As.).
english_raw: A trickster cannot trick the barber. To boastful trickster.

igbo_raw: Akbata si n' aiya n' ekwu orhu na nnq mwa dinweniye adamwa (As.).
english_raw: The guitar says that he speaks 20 and 400, but his owner does not know. In a quarrel when a young man boasts of his progress.

igbo_raw: Ony' âmala adainya n' ply (As.).
english_raw: The paddler does not paddle in the mud. Of one who talks of self " against another." One leg does not stand up. If two men begin title and only one finishes and boasts, other replies, you had backers.

igbo_raw: Nnono adefe nke obwana Ako (0.0.).
english_raw: Bird does not fly as egret, child of Ako. To boaster-cannot be richer than king.

igbo_raw: Ofu onye adew' yzo n' yzg nabg (0.0.).
english_raw: One man does not stand in two roads. To a man who boasts of many children (it takes woman also).

igbo_raw: Osisi odaka onwala mma (0.0.).
english_raw: No tree is finer than onwala. To boaster who has no wife or child.

igbo_raw: Ainyanwu Stòtò akgn' äkwä; nk' ainyase bu abwolo
english_raw: (0.0.). The sun of the morning does not dry clothes; the evening sun is weak (not strong enough to dry). When a man who has not worked at all boasts of when he will finish.

igbo_raw: Ágo bp ony' pma, ggazu by ony' oma, ago çbu ggazu bu ggazu nkili (Ala).
english_raw: The leopard is a good creature, the guinea fowl is too; the leopard kills the guinea fowl and keeps looking at it. When rivals try to eclipse each other and spoil each other's show.

igbo_raw: Onye Agolo si eyi: ebwanarhia obu ngina (? mu) n'ani Agolo; ebwana rhirhga, obu ngina (mu) n'ani Agolo (As.).
english_raw: and me in town of Agolo; if you do not run, it is you and me in Agolo. If two boasters meet, "wait till year comes."

igbo_raw: Nkite amateta ola Stoto zizipu nto; ebe omatorò ute, ainyase alarokwa na nto (Uk.).
english_raw: Dog does not wake in morning and shake off ashes; but if it does not order mat, in the evening it sleeps in the ashes again. Of idle boasting of man who has done nothing.

igbo_raw: Onyê n'üce, ónyê n'ücê (0.0.).
english_raw: Who has his opinion, has his opinion. To obstinate man.

igbo_raw: Mwa we mw' aka ndu pia ony aka (Ubul.).
english_raw: I can't crush my hand because of insects. Refusal.

igbo_raw: K'imwak' ife, imwago ijiji benyà (0.0.).
english_raw: As you know a thing, did you know the fly of yesterday (used especially by women). If woman refuses, e.g., salt to one from whom she borrows often.

igbo_raw: Ogoli 'mwaká, qdany onwê (Alá).
english_raw: Woman is fine, does not marry herself. Girl who refuses suitors.

igbo_raw: Orhte amw'afie mbwada, atabe aka; mwa cify niya gafy (Uk.).
english_raw: A hunter misses duiker, bites finger; at dawn next day he will see it. When man's request is refused.

igbo_raw: Qsá si enunkwu zidete, si plili gekbenye ekwele (Ubul.).
english_raw: Squirrel comes down from palm says to ground squirrel: go and get me cord (from tree). Refusal to do what is requested.

igbo_raw: Anum nafa naëy aja ofu obwe, mwa nke obwe nabo amwozinam (Ubul.).
english_raw: I hear they make sacrifice for bad travelling, but for coming back I don't know. One thing at a time (?) Refusal to fall in with suggestion. Ofu obwe is diviner's language.

igbo_raw: Efi si na osoiya osg cjenye qkene ije naiya da pleng amabuye (Ubul.).
english_raw: The cow says it pleases her to walk with traders; if she falls the traders will not carry her. Refusal to accompany messenger.

igbo_raw: Wadaju onye k' osi kg ntoa (Ubul.).
english_raw: They don't ask one how he scratches his sore. A man who refuses to cease at bidding.

igbo_raw: Owu dj n'isi K'eyi jille omangâna (As.).
english_raw: Fame is on the head as rat takes name of gmangana (one who sits in one place). If lame man, e.g., is successful.

igbo_raw: Ogoli d'Odò naiyasi ngnibe diye (Ala).
english_raw: A woman is quiet because she alone is in husband's house. People interfere only with successful man,

igbo_raw: Nkiti qsa Bume akwu, qsa ásana ike piju фdodo (Ubul.).
english_raw: Ever since the squirrel cut nuts it has never been able to fill calabash with oil. Of an unsuccessful man who works hard.

igbo_raw: Ainya adigo kainye grwe mwainya, onebo onye ganata eiwe dbwd (As.).
english_raw: It is fitting to give palm wine to a monkey; but who will bring the calabash back? When a farmer sees he succeeds less than a man who planted less.

igbo_raw: Omem n' amwanam; mwa mwale gini kangeme (0.0.).
english_raw: He troubles me because I did not know; if I had known what should I have done ? Unsuccessful man tries various plans.

igbo_raw: Wadeji ikobi esi okwa mwa mili ngo ádjna (I,A.).
english_raw: They never try hard to cook okwa if water of ngo (lye) is not in it. One can try hard for riches, but fail if it is not his lot.

igbo_raw: Mili obwana ji wy ary k'ugo jinyaica ary; nk'ugo abal'ugo nife (As.).
english_raw: Water egret takes wash body, is the same that cagle takes wash (with soap) body ; ugo's water is gain for him. One's labour is useless, another's fruitful.

igbo_raw: Óté ainya bia n'isi (0.0.).
english_raw: It is long when the eye comes to the head. Of long and fruitless discussion- postponement.

igbo_raw: Yalo ebwe kebwe w'ebe pkuti (Ubul.).
english_raw: Leave ebwe (tree), let it stand where it stands. Postponing action (if one is in trouble).

igbo_raw: UzQ d'owu, nduli ekol' akba (As.).
english_raw: Road is cool, dove takes up bag. To unwelcome or inconvenient visitor; " come another time," when man has other business and postpones caller.

igbo_raw: Osq si nne n'im'oka gamyya, yamunye n'afg (As.).
english_raw: Bat tells mother while in womb, if she delays to deliver her, she will bear her own child in womb. To procrastinator.

igbo_raw: Onwu dikeBu nw' okete, ogelugo ka nnenkwu (Ala).
english_raw: If the young oil palm does not die, it will grow big. Children will grow up.

igbo_raw: Okenye sosie, ocg ibe (0.0.).

These tests were only roughly applied and in the light of further results, I feel some doubt as to how far they were accurate. As, however, my later enquiries dealt with the Asaba language, whereas the tests in question were applied to utterances of natives of Awka and Abg, it does not follow that the results of the latter were necessarily wrong. The main difference that appears is a much greater interval between the high tones and the low tones in Asaba. The low tones appear to have been accurately determined at C, but at Asaba the high tones appear to be at least five semi- tones above the previous datum. In the case of single words the pitch was determined without any trouble by means of a tuning fork. This applies whether the tone was simple or compound. In certain cases, however, such as gze, king, which as an individual word I had, independently of phonograph records, been disposed to regard as a two-four word, that is to say a word with the second tone on the first syllable and the fourth tone on the second syllable, the phonograph record shows that the actual pitch is E for the first syllable and G below for the second. If we take the àkwà, bed, which is usually regarded as having two low tones, but actually has a falling tone on the first syllable and a low tone on the second, we find that the low tone of the second is C. The question therefore arises whether the low tone of eze is the same as the low tone of akwa, and is only lowered on account of its position in the sentence, or whether we must distinguish a tone below C. The material at my disposal does not enable mne to say which solution is correct; but wg (this) has a falling tone to the same note. As regards the middle tones, a kwa, egg, is A and Ab, or, in an interrogative sentence, G and B; akwa, cloth, is G and A in an interrogative sentence or (GG#) and G_ in an affirma- tive one. In the absence of further material it hardly appears possible to reach any defimite conclusion on the subject of the number of the middle tones. If we assume that all the tones mentioned above are identical and that the C of the second syllable in àk wà is really a middle tone, the low tone being properly G, as in the second syllable of eze, we may then regard the middle tone as having a high component varying in pitch between F and A, and a low component varying in pitch between B and D. If we now turn to falling tones, we find a small fall from D to C in the first syllable of äkwà, bed, in interrogative sentences; and in affirmative sentences the fall is from E to ©; in the second syllable of ago, leopard, the fall is from A to G#. It may, however, be repeated that the number of instances is exceedingly small; in the case of the demonstrative adjective, w,o, the example was taken from a sentence, and the pitch may, therefore, have been influenced by phrase tone. At the same time it may be remarked that the falling tone in wp is almost identical with the two tones found in the word gze.
